questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Vehicles will enter the roadway ahead.
Traffic signal ahead.
Stop completely. Then go when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely. Then go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: Red octagonal signs are always stop signs. You must come to a complete stop, check for other traffic and pedestrians, and proceed only when safe.

questions.question: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield:

options.text: Protects your face, but not your eyes.
Protects your eyes, but not your whole face.
Protects your whole face.

questions.correctAnswerText: Protects your whole face.
questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your entire face and eyes in a crash. A windshield does not provide the same protection.

questions.question: When crossing angled railroad tracks, it is usually best to:

options.text: Use the road shoulder to slow down before crossing the tracks.
Walk your motorcycle across the tracks.
Go straight through your lane to cross the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Go straight through your lane to cross the tracks.
questions.explanation: Ride straight across angled railroad or trolley tracks. Changing your angle may move you into another lane and cause a crash with oncoming traffic.

questions.question: Reflective, brightly-colored helmets and clothing:

options.text: Should only be worn when riding at night.
Help make motorcycle riders more visible.
Do not improve a motorcycle rider's safety.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help make motorcycle riders more visible.
questions.explanation: Wearing brightly-colored or reflective clothing helps other drivers see you on the road.

questions.question: When being passed, moving to the far side of your lane away from the passing vehicle:

options.text: Is recommended because you will be farther from the passing vehicle.
Is not recommended because it may cause the other driver to move back into your lane too soon.
Does not affect safety either way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is not recommended because it may cause the other driver to move back into your lane too soon.
questions.explanation: Do not move to the far side of your lane when being passed. Doing so may encourage the other driver to return to your lane too early.

questions.question: If you reach an uncontrolled intersection at the same time as another vehicle:

options.text: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
Flash your headlight to signal the other vehicle to go.
Continue through and expect the other vehicle to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
questions.explanation: At an uncontrolled intersection with no signs or traffic lights, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Traffic signal ahead
Intersection ahead
Divided roadway ahead

questions.correctAnswerText: Divided roadway ahead
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. This sign warns you that the road ahead is divided.

questions.question: When approaching an intersection, a motorcyclist should not:

options.text: Choose a lane position that makes them more visible.
Speed up to cross the intersection quickly.
Cover the clutch and brakes to react faster.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up to cross the intersection quickly.
questions.explanation: As you approach an intersection, choose a visible lane position and cover the clutch and brakes to react quickly. Slow down as you approach. Do not make sudden speed or position changes, as other drivers may misunderstand your actions.

questions.question: Which of the following is a slippery surface?

options.text: A gravel road
A paved driveway
Dry pavement

questions.correctAnswerText: A gravel road
questions.explanation: Poor traction surfaces include wet, snowy, icy, or muddy pavement; gravel roads; lane markings; and metal plates and utility hole covers.

questions.question: When passing parked vehicles, a motorcycle rider has an advantage over a car driver because:

options.text: The motorcycle can speed up more quickly than a car.
The motorcyclist can ride on the left side of the lane to avoid doors, drivers, and pedestrians on the right.
Motorcycles stop shorter than cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: The motorcyclist can ride on the left side of the lane to avoid doors, drivers, and pedestrians on the right.
questions.explanation: When passing parked vehicles on your right, ride in the left portion of your lane. This helps you avoid opening doors, drivers getting out, or people stepping from between vehicles. Only do this if there is no oncoming traffic.

questions.question: For eye or face shield protection to work well, it must:

options.text: Fit securely in place.
Block your side vision so you focus on the road ahead.
Not allow eyeglasses or sunglasses to be worn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fit securely in place.
questions.explanation: Good eye or face shield protection must be free of scratches, resist damage, allow clear side views, fit securely, let air through to prevent fogging, and allow room for eyeglasses or sunglasses.

questions.question: Why should a motorcyclist not rely only on mirrors?

options.text: Mirrors can get dirty and block the view.
Mirrors are always unreliable.
Motorcycles have blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: Motorcycles have blind spots.
questions.explanation: Mirrors alone are not enough to stay aware of your surroundings. Motorcycles have blind spots like all vehicles.

questions.question: When other vehicles are slowed or stopped, a motorcyclist should:

options.text: Not weave between lanes of traffic.
Weave in and out of traffic lanes.
Ride in a straight line between two lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not weave between lanes of traffic.
questions.explanation: Riding between stopped or slow-moving vehicles is dangerous. Other vehicles may change lanes, doors may open, or arms may stick out. Motorcycles need a full lane to operate safely.

questions.question: Smaller vehicles appear to be ________ and slower than they really are.

options.text: Closer
Farther away
Larger

questions.correctAnswerText: Farther away
questions.explanation: It is hard to judge the speed and distance of small vehicles like motorcycles. Do not assume that drivers of larger vehicles can accurately judge your speed and location.

questions.question: Taking a turn too fast can cause a rider to:

options.text: Cross into another lane of traffic.
Get through the turn faster.
Keep control of their motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cross into another lane of traffic.
questions.explanation: Taking a turn too fast may cause a rider to cross into another lane or leave the road. Slow down before entering a turn or curve.

questions.question: When starting your motorcycle, the engine should be in:

options.text: First gear.
Neutral.
Third gear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Neutral.
questions.explanation: Make sure your motorcycle's transmission is in neutral before starting the engine. Most motorcycles have a neutral light on the speedometer that turns on when the ignition is on and the bike is in neutral.

questions.question: Before every ride, you should:

options.text: Make sure your bike's brake lights work.
Make sure the paint on the bike is not peeling.
Make sure your bike is completely clean.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure your bike's brake lights work.
questions.explanation: Check your motorcycle's safety before every ride. Test your brake controls to make sure each one activates the brake lights.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No right turn
No left turn
No U-turn

questions.correctAnswerText: No U-turn
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs are white with red and black markings. They tell drivers about traffic laws in that area. This sign means U-turns are not allowed.

questions.question: When motorcyclists ride in a group, inexperienced riders should:

options.text: Lead the group.
Be near the front of the group.
Be in the back of the group.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be near the front of the group.
questions.explanation: Less experienced riders should be placed near the front of the group behind the leader. This allows experienced riders to lead and watch the less experienced riders at the same time.

questions.question: If your front wheel locks while braking, you should:

options.text: Keep the tire locked until your next stop.
Continue squeezing the front brake lever.
Release the front brake and immediately re-apply it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the front brake and immediately re-apply it.
questions.explanation: If the front wheel locks while braking, release the brake pressure. Then re-apply it with controlled, gradual pressure.

questions.question: A passenger on a motorcycle should:

options.text: Put their feet on the ground when the motorcycle stops.
Not ride without a back rest.
Sit as far forward as possible without crowding the driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sit as far forward as possible without crowding the driver.
questions.explanation: A passenger should sit as far forward as possible without crowding the driver. Keep both feet on the footrests at all times, even when stopped.

questions.question: To reduce your chances of a crash, you should do all of the following except:

options.text: Look ahead at your path.
Be ready to act to avoid a hazard.
Turn your headlight off during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your headlight off during the day.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, always make sure other drivers can see you. Use your signals, brake light, and lane position to communicate. Keep space around your motorcycle and always scan the road ahead, behind, and next to you.

questions.question: Which lane position is best for preventing other vehicles from sharing your lane?

options.text: The left portion of the lane
The center portion of the lane
The right portion of the lane

questions.correctAnswerText: The center portion of the lane
questions.explanation: Riding in the center portion of your lane discourages other drivers from squeezing into your lane. When traveling behind a car, riding in the center also places you in the middle of their rearview mirror, where they are most likely to see you.

questions.question: As you approach a blind intersection, you should:

options.text: Move to the part of the lane where other drivers can see you most easily.
Move to the part of the lane closest to the traffic sign or light.
Move to the outside edge of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the part of the lane where other drivers can see you most easily.
questions.explanation: At a blind intersection, move to the part of the lane that puts you in the view of other drivers as soon as possible.

questions.question: When riding behind a car in the left third of the lane, the driver can see you in their side mirror. What is a problem with this?

options.text: Most drivers don't check their side mirrors as often as their rearview mirror.
Wind may prevent the driver from using their side mirror.
Drivers should not use their side mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Most drivers don't check their side mirrors as often as their rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Most drivers look at their rearview mirror more often than their side mirrors. When following a car, ride in the center portion of the lane where the driver is most likely to see you in their rearview mirror.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Yield
Slow-moving vehicle
Railroad crossing

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow-moving vehicle
questions.explanation: This sign is on the back of slow-moving vehicles traveling below 25 mph, such as farm equipment, construction vehicles, or horse-drawn wagons.

questions.question: You should flash your brake light to:

options.text: Tell other drivers that you are riding near them.
Help other drivers see your motorcycle in slow traffic.
Warn other drivers that you will slow down or stop where they don't expect it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Warn other drivers that you will slow down or stop where they don't expect it.
questions.explanation: Use your brake light to communicate with other drivers. Flash it before making a sharp, fast turn off a high-speed road or when slowing anywhere drivers may not expect it.

questions.question: It is illegal to operate a motorcycle with a blood alcohol content (BAC) of:

options.text: 0.08 percent or higher.
0.1 percent or higher.
0.3 percent or higher.

questions.correctAnswerText: 0.08 percent or higher.
questions.explanation: In California, people age 21 or older cannot operate a motorcycle with a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher. People under 21 cannot operate with a BAC of 0.01 percent or higher. Riding may be unsafe even below the legal limit.

questions.question: The Motorcycle Safety Foundation recommends a SEE strategy for safe riding. What does "SEE" stand for?

options.text: Search, Evaluate, and Execute.
Slow, Experienced, and Error-free.
Safe, Experienced, and Evasive.

questions.correctAnswerText: Search, Evaluate, and Execute.
questions.explanation: Experienced riders use the SEE strategy to make safe decisions. "SEE" stands for Search, Evaluate, and Execute.

questions.question: Convex mirrors:

options.text: Show a narrow view of the road behind you.
Show a wide view of the road behind you.
Are illegal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Show a wide view of the road behind you.
questions.explanation: Convex mirrors show a wider view than flat mirrors. They also make objects look farther away than they really are. Take time to adjust to convex mirrors on your motorcycle.
